content: Nice puzzle. I'm ashamed of how long it took me to realise that the capitalisation was relevant. Considering that you've got 9 case pairs, it might be nice to bring it up to a round number with a case that includes no capitalisation (maybe no numbers too) for an additional hint at the end. You could make the input string lowercase names from the leaderboard to stick with your theme. Probably fine as is, just thought I'd put it out there.

I'm honoured to be included in the cases, and I'll take the remark as a compliment 😊

Cases
* Validator 1 (jayem94) seems to be better paired with Test 5 (user123), as both usernames contain a multiple-digit number.

* After swapping the cases, Validator 1 would be better replaced with a username containing single digits.

* Since the cases should be ordered from easy to complex, it may be better to include my username, along with other usernames containing digits, later. Or perhaps you could share with us the current logic behind how the cases are ordered, or the scenario that each case pair is intended to cover?

* It's interesting that all validators except Validator 3 are restricted to the usernames of Clash of Code bots. Actually, Pair 3 works better as the first (example) pair. I'm just not sure whether Test 3 gives away too much (e.g. on how capitalisation is relevant or what transformation is required), though. Does @Sflubaduba have any thoughts on that?

Thanks.

I think swapping pairs 1 and 3 is a good idea. It's still a bit of a challenge to figure out. To be honest, I looked at test 3, thought about the capitalised letters and brushed it off because the alphabetical shift was inverted.

I swapped JayEm94 with Tychkorg and putted a zero at the end of Tychkorg's output so it has a single digit.

There was no logic behind the order of the cases because when I submitted this contribution it was 11PM here :P

Aside from @User123 and @5DN1L, the usernames are from people that I've played with or seen frequently in clashes, and the outputs are compliments or sentences that reminds the user in a good way.

I don't want to include a pair with no lowercase & no digit because the output would be blank, and I don't want to add one more condition to handle blank output, like printing "NONE" or "BLANK". But, if necessary, I can add one more hint where the input mention uppercase letters.
I don't know if it was necessary, but all inputs from tests and validators cover all letters from the English alphabet.
I moved the hint to be the first test case.

Oh my gosh @Sflubaduba thanks for pointing the inverted alphabetical shift. This was not intended.

I coded a generator to make the inputs and didn't realize that the shifts were backwards.

I updated all test cases and the solution. The shifts should be added, not subtracted.

Awesome
That should make it a bit more obvious.

Interesting. I thought that in some cases the result might fall beyond either end of the alphabet, so modulo might be needed, but it turns out the result always stays within bounds.

My username is the only one where digits appear both at the beginning and in the middle. In all the other usernames you've chosen that contain digits, the digits appear only at the end (well, @Tychkorg's name doesn't really contain any digits…). That's the only issue I can spot.

By the way, I browsed through Page 1 of the Clash of Code leaderboard, sorted by decreasing number of clashes played. It shows a few usernames where digits appear either at the beginning or in the middle, but not both.

https://www.codingame.com/leaderboards/clash/global?column=clashescount&value=DECREASING

There is the user @21stCenturyPeon. The 2 appears at the beginning and the 1 doesn't appear at the beginning or end, so middle?

I may put this user as the validator of your username. This will break the player/bot pattern but your username definitely can't be out of the list.

I putted the 0 at the end of @Tychkorg's name 'cause since it's a validator, I didn't care much for the bot.
